FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic keeps right, passing goes left as the norm and right only when necessary and safe, hazard-avoiding moves stay minimal, and no pass may break the speed limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Passed motorcycles keep their whole lane width, and no car may share lane space with one however wide the lane or one-sided the bike. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Passed cyclists get sufficient room, with rear overtakes going left at a safe distance until the bicycle clears. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Lane changes need lamp or hand signals at least one hundred feet ahead, and no driver may pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Left passes die on solid yellow center lines, unreturnable gaps before a far solid line, oncoming traffic inside two hundred feet, blind curves and hillcrests on two-way roads, within one hundred feet of two-way railroad crossings, within one hundred feet of obstructed two-way bridges, tunnels and viaducts, and whenever oncoming traffic would suffer interference. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Passing drivers mirror-check, signal, and left-shoulder-check the blind spot that mirrors miss before entering the left lane, then signal, confirm the passed bumper in the rear-view mirror plus pavement over the right shoulder, and return right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
Right passes are allowed only past a left-turning vehicle ahead, on two-way roads marked or wide enough for two-plus lanes each way without prohibitions or obstructions, and never across shoulders or edge lines except by sign or officer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
Right passes are also allowed on one-way roads marked or wide enough for two-plus lanes without prohibitions or obstructions, with intersection passes checking ahead for left-turning vehicles and rightward for pedestrians, cyclists, skaters and moped riders. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A02
School buses telegraph stops with yellow roof flashers front and back, commanding slower speed and stop readiness. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
Passed drivers slow slightly, hold lane center, and resume speed once clear, while chronic right-side passing means moving right to free the left lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
Red-flashing stopped school buses halt both-direction traffic everywhere including school grounds and lots, stopping at least twenty feet back, identified by the school-bus sign, roof reds and yellow-orange paint. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Stopped drivers wait until the bus rolls or the driver or an officer waves them on, on every New York roadway including the far side of divided highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
After the bus stop, drivers scan roadside children and creep past them, since most bus deaths strike crossing children rather than bus occupants. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
Disability-transport vehicles built as school buses command identical stops. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A02
Passing a stopped school bus fines two hundred fifty dollars first, up to one thousand for three violations in three years, with three-in-three-years revoking the license at least six months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
The twenty-nineteen stop-arm-camera law lets districts and towns bill owners passing red-flashing stopped buses two hundred fifty dollars first, two hundred seventy-five second within eighteen months, and three hundred third and beyond within eighteen months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A03
The chapter closes with review questions on passing side, pre-pass checks, the mirror check before returning, right-pass conditions, the crosswalk-stop rule, being passed, and bus warning lights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=41]
